title: How many right angles are in the windows of your classroom?
description: One rectangular window pane is looked at, and each of its corners is seen to be a right angle. The panes are counted, and other corners in the classroom are searched for. A square corner of folded paper is fitted into one corner as the check.
teaching_notes: One idea: every corner of a rectangular pane is a right angle, so the count is the corners of one pane times the number of panes. Watch for students who count only the panes and forget the corners.

video_script.why: The child finds right angles in the windows of a classroom by counting the corners of one pane.
video_script.substitution: the windows of the child's own classroom, with a rectangular pane drawn on the board
video_script.anchor: a classroom window with its rectangular panes
video_script.payoff_line: Each rectangular pane has four right angles, one at each corner

final_answer.value: it depends on the classroom; each rectangular pane has 4 right angles, and doors, desks, board corners and book corners have more
final_answer.spoken: it depends on the classroom, but each rectangular pane has four right angles, and doors, desks, boards and books have more

hold_back: Each rectangular pane has four right angles
maths_rules: a right angle looks like the letter L and is a quarter of a full turn
a rectangular pane has 4 corners, and each corner is a right angle, so 4 right angles per pane
total for the windows = 4 times the number of panes, which depends on the classroom
other right angles: corners of the board, door, desks and books
check: fit the corner of a folded paper, a right angle, into a corner of the pane
video_script.design: One idea: count the corners of one pane, then count the panes. One drawn pane stays on the board.
open_questions: The total depends on the child's own classroom, so the video gives the counting method and the four right angles per rectangular pane only.
